title: Directions & getting around
description: Ask where things are, understand directions and guide an auto or cab driver.

guide.title: Where is ...? How far?
guide.text:
'Where is X?' is X + ಎಲ್ಲಿದೆ? (ellide?), which is elli 'where' + ide 'is'. For a person use elliddaare?

'How far?' is ಎಷ್ಟು ದೂರ? (eshtu doora?). 'From here' is ಇಲ್ಲಿಂದ (illinda). 'Near' is ಹತ್ತಿರ (hattira); 'far' is ದೂರ (doora).

Answers you will hear: ಇಲ್ಲೇ (ille) right here; ಹತ್ತಿರದಲ್ಲೇ (hattiradalle) very near; ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ದೂರ (svalpa doora) a bit far; ಎರಡು ಕಿಲೋಮೀಟರ್ (eradu kilomeetar) two kilometres; ಐದು ನಿಮಿಷ (aidu nimisha) five minutes.

Place names take -ge or -kke for 'to': maisoorige, jayanagarakke, steshange. English place words ending in a consonant simply add -ge in speech.

examples.english: How far is it from here?

guide.title: Left, right, straight
guide.text:
ಎಡ (eda) is 'left' and ಬಲ (bala) is 'right'. With the 'to' ending they become ಎಡಕ್ಕೆ (edakke) 'to the left' and ಬಲಕ್ಕೆ (balakke) 'to the right'. 'On the left side' is ಎಡಗಡೆ (edagade), 'on the right side' ಬಲಗಡೆ (balagade). In Bengaluru drivers very often use the English words left and right, with Kannada verbs.

ನೇರವಾಗಿ (neravaagi) or ನೇರ (nera) is 'straight'. ಮುಂದೆ (munde) is 'ahead, in front'; ಹಿಂದೆ (hinde) 'behind, back'; ಪಕ್ಕ (pakka) 'beside, next to'; ಎದುರು (eduru) 'opposite'.

Verbs: ಹೋಗಿ (hogi) go; ತಿರುಗಿ (tirugi) turn; ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸಿ (nillisi) stop (the vehicle); ಬನ್ನಿ (banni) come.

guide.title: Autos, cabs and buses
guide.text:
To hail an auto-rickshaw, name the place with -ge / -kke and ask ಬರ್ತೀರಾ? (barteeraa?), 'will you come?': mejestikge barteeraa? The driver answers banni ('come') or names a price.

ಮೀಟರ್ ಹಾಕಿ (meetar haaki) is 'put the meter on'. ಎಷ್ಟು ಆಗುತ್ತೆ? (eshtu aagutte?) is 'how much will it come to?'.

'I want to go to X' is naanu X-ge hogabeku. On a bus, ask the conductor: ee bas X-ge hoguttaa? 'does this bus go to X?'. To get off, say illi ilisi, 'let me down here'.

ಇಳಿ (ili) is 'get down, get off' and ಹತ್ತು (hattu) is 'climb, get on' - yes, the same word as 'ten'.

examples.english: I want to go to the airport.

phrases.note: The formal Kannada word is railu nildaana (ರೈಲು ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ).
A large bus station is bas styaand (ಬಸ್ ಸ್ಟ್ಯಾಂಡ್).

phrases.english: How far is it from here?

phrases.note: Both the e in ne and the o in ho are long.
Said to a driver. nillisu = to stop something; nillu = to stop, stand.

phrases.english: I want to go to the airport.
phrases.note: In everyday speech people usually just say 'airport': erportge (ಏರ್‌ಪೋರ್ಟ್‌ಗೆ).
How to ask an auto driver. Majestic is Bengaluru's central bus and rail hub.
In cities people often say 'toilet ellide?'
Adding -aa to the end of a sentence makes it a yes/no question.
nadedukondu hogu = to go on foot. Spoken: nadkondu (ನಡ್ಕೊಂಡು).
